cohort: Five women diagnosed with newly metastatic or relapsed BRAF V600E-mutated pregnancy-associated melanoma (four during gestation and one in the 1st year postpartum) between 2012 and 2019.
finding: All five women with BRAF V600E-mutated PAM developed extensive metastatic disease, experienced rapid melanoma progression in less than 6 months, and died soon after diagnosis, suggesting a detrimental effect of BRAF-mutated status on disease outcome.
followup_time: Up to 2 years after birth for neonates (one developed melanoma earlier than the second year of life), and less than 6 months for melanoma progression in mothers.
